title: Salmon and Dill Pie
subtitle: Fresh salmon in a cream and dill sauce under golden puff pastry
excerpt: Salmon and dill pie uses fresh salmon in a light cream sauce fragrant with dill under a puff pastry lid. The salmon stays tender and pink, the dill keeps the sauce fresh rather than heavy. It is a less robust but more elegant fish pie than the smoked-fish versions, suited to spring and summer.
sourceNotes: Salmon and dill is a classic pairing in British and Scandinavian cooking. The combination appears in both hot dishes and cold preparations, where the dill cuts through the richness of the fish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead, refrigerate. Top and bake on the day.

glossaryTerms.definition: A feathery herb with a fresh, anise-adjacent flavour. Widely used with fish and in cream sauces. Add it at the end of cooking to preserve its character.

content.text: Salmon and dill pie is lighter in character than most British meat pies. The salmon poaches gently in stock, stays in large flakes, and sits in a cream sauce that is kept fresh with lemon and
. The whole thing bakes under puff pastry for 25 minutes. Do not overcook the salmon during poaching: it finishes in the oven inside the pie.

Put {{salmon-fillet}} of salmon in a pan with {{stock-chicken}} of stock. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and poach for 5 minutes until barely opaque at the centre. The salmon will finish cooking in the oven. Lift out and break into large flakes. Reserve the poaching stock.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a pan over medium heat. Add {{leek}} sliced leeks and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in {{plain-flour}} of flour and cook for 1 minute. Whisk in the warm reserved stock, then {{double-cream}} of double cream. Simmer until thick, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the dill fronds, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season well.
Gently fold the salmon flakes into the sauce. Transfer to the pie dish and cool for 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Brush the rim of the dish with beaten egg. Lay the puff pastry over the filling, seal the edges, and trim. Cut a steam vent. Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.

items.symptom: The salmon is dry and overcooked
items.cause: It was poached through before baking, then cooked again in the oven.
items.fix: Poach for 5 minutes only, leaving the centre translucent. The salmon finishes in the oven and will be tender when the pie is done.

items.cause: Dill was added too early and cooked out.
items.fix: Add the dill after the sauce is off the heat. It needs only the residual warmth to bloom, not direct heat.

items.cause: Too much lemon juice was added.
items.fix: Use the zest of the whole lemon but add the juice in stages. A small amount of lemon lifts the sauce; too much makes it acidic.

items.cause: The sauce was too thin and did not hold the fish together.
items.fix: The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon before the fish is folded in. Simmer longer if needed before removing from the heat.

content.text: Salmon and dill is a pairing with roots in Scandinavian cooking that was absorbed fully into British cuisine, particularly in Scotland, where wild Atlantic salmon has always been part of the landscape. As a pie, it is elegant enough for a dinner party and straightforward enough for a weeknight supper. Serve with new potatoes and peas in spring, or with a green salad when the weather is warmer.
